name: Incredible
tagline: Your Android phone, linked to your Mac.
description: Incredible connects an Android phone to a Mac over your local network. Traffic is encrypted end to end with a key shared once by QR code. There is no account, cloud service or server.

platforms.note: Not notarized. After the first launch is blocked, allow it in System Settings, Privacy & Security.

features.title: Notifications
features.text: Banners on the Mac, with dismiss synced both ways, action buttons and inline reply.

features.title: Calls
features.text: Answer, decline, hang up and dial from a floating panel. Call audio stays on the phone.

features.title: Files and photos
features.text: Move files over USB cable, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and drag recent photos to Finder.

features.title: Clipboard and links
features.text: Mac clipboard reaches the phone automatically, and links open on either side.

features.title: Media
features.text: See what's playing, with playback controls and phone volume.

features.title: Phone status
features.text: Battery, network, signal, storage, ringer and volume at a glance.

features.title: Find My Phone
features.text: Rings at full alarm volume, even on silent.

setup: Install the app on both the Mac and the phone, and keep them on the same network.
On the Mac, choose Show Pairing Code.
In the phone app, choose Scan code, then confirm.
In the phone app, tap Enable for each feature you want.
Allow notifications when the Mac asks.
limits: If Android blocks notification access with "Restricted setting", open the app's page in system Settings, then the ⋮ menu, then Allow restricted settings.
Treat the pairing code like a password. Anyone who has it can read what your phone sends.
It works on a local network or within Bluetooth range, not between networks.
SMS only. RCS chats appear as notifications instead.
